transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’m here because ever since my father-in-law moved in, I haven’t really been myself. I’m snapping at my wife over little things around the house, and I keep putting off jobs and paperwork I used to stay on top of. Even when I’m out in the workshop or trying to fish, I just can’t seem to get my head quiet.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge since your father-in-law moved in?

Yeah, I guess I have. Since he moved in, I just feel wound up a lot of the time. I snap at my wife over small stuff around the house, and I keep putting off things I’d normally handle. Even when I’m trying to relax in the workshop or go fishing, my head just won’t quiet down.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time since your father-in-law moved in?
I don’t think I’d say sad most of the time. I mean, I get frustrated and worn down, but I haven’t really noticed being down all day or anything like that.
Do you find yourself worrying about things most of the time?

Yeah, I do. It’s like my head just keeps going, even when I’m doing something that’s supposed to calm me down, like being out in the workshop or fishing. Since my father-in-law moved in, I’ve been worrying and getting worked up over stuff around the house more than I used to.
Do you find yourself having repetitive thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head?

Yeah, I guess so. It’s not like one exact thought over and over, but my mind keeps circling back to the same stuff at home since my father-in-law moved in. I’ll be in the workshop or trying to fish, and I still can’t get my head quiet. Then I end up snapping at my wife over little things or putting off things I normally handle.
Have you been avoiding any activities or places since your father-in-law moved in?
I’m not sure I’d say I’ve been avoiding places, exactly. I haven’t really noticed staying away from anything specific since he moved in.
Have you been enjoying things you usually like to do since your father-in-law moved in?

Not as much, no. I still go out to the workshop or try to fish, but I can’t really settle into it like I used to. My head keeps running over things at home since my father-in-law moved in, and I end up getting tense instead of enjoying it.
Do you feel like you've been in a low mood most of the time since your father-in-law moved in?
I don’t know if I’d say low most of the time. I’ve been stressed and worn down by it, but I haven’t really noticed being sad all day or anything like that.
Have you noticed any change in your weight since your father-in-law moved in?
Not really. I haven’t noticed my weight changing much since he moved in.
Do you worry about things even when there's no apparent reason to worry?
I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I do worry, but it usually feels tied to what’s going on at home. It’s not like I’m worrying for no reason all the time.
Do you find yourself worrying about things even when they are not happening or are unlikely to happen?
Not really. I mean, I worry about the situation at home, but I don’t usually catch myself worrying about things that aren’t happening or probably won’t happen.
Do you worry about a wide range of things, not just your father-in-law moving in?
I don’t think so. It’s mostly centered on him being in the house and how that’s been affecting things. I’m not usually worrying about a whole bunch of different things.
Have you been having trouble sleeping since your father-in-law moved in?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been paying close attention to my sleep, so I can’t say for sure that it changed because of him moving in.
Do you worry about everyday things like finances, health, or relationships even when they are going well?

I haven’t really noticed that, no. I mean, I can worry about normal stuff when there’s a reason, but I don’t think I’m sitting around worrying about finances or health or relationships when they’re going okay.
Do you often find yourself worrying about everyday things like work, chores, or minor matters even when there's nothing specifically bothering you?
No, not really. I don’t usually find myself worrying about little everyday things if there isn’t something specific going on.
Do you think your worry about your father-in-law moving in is greater than would be expected for someone in your situation?

Yeah… I think maybe it is more than it should be. Since he moved in, I’ve been snapping at my wife over little things around the house, and I keep putting off jobs and paperwork I used to just handle. Even when I’m out in the workshop or trying to fish, I can’t seem to get my head quiet. So it feels like it’s gotten bigger than just normal stress.
Do you find that you're worrying about your father-in-law and the situation at home even when you're not there?

Yeah, I do. Even when I’m not home, it’s kind of still there in the back of my mind. Like if I’m in the workshop or trying to go fishing, I can’t really settle down or get my head quiet. It keeps coming back to him being there and how things are going at home.
Has your worry about your father-in-law moving in interfered with your ability to function at work or in other areas of your life?

Yes, it has. I’m not working a regular job right now, but I do small repair jobs, and I’ve had to turn some down or delay them because I’m just not keeping up like I used to. I also missed an important contractor-license filing date, which isn’t like me.

And at home, it’s caused a lot of tension with my wife. I’m having a harder time following through on things I’m supposed to handle for the family.
Do you feel compelled to repeat certain actions or behaviors over and over?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I might put things off or go back over something in my head, but I don’t have any behaviors I feel like I have to repeat over and over.
Have you experienced significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning since your father-in-law moved in?

Yes. It’s definitely affected things. I missed an important contractor-license filing date, which I normally would’ve stayed on top of. And I’ve had to turn down or push back some small repair jobs because I’m just not keeping up like I used to.

At home, it’s put a real strain on my marriage, and I’m having a harder time following through on the things I’m supposed to do for the family.
